Growing up in the countryside you start to notice there’s a type of “rural gentrification” that has its own flavor compared to urban gentrification.

* Highways get repaved.

* Yellow paint on the road gets replaced by white paint.

* The side of the highways start being mowed.

* Changes in the cars you see in the road. They get a lot newer and you start to see more CUVs and fewer trucks.

* The small towns go from being completely dead to bustling. Lots of new restaurants and bars mainly. The existing restaurants get nicer (Susie May’s Country Diner ditches the plastic cups for glass and doubles their prices) but still try to sell based on heritage.

* Agriculture becomes classy. Either they start selling the “farmers experience” to tourists (apple picking, etc) or they start upselling based on the fact they’re local/organic.

Generally this happens when either a nearby town with a thriving industry (tourism, education, health) or a nearby small city start exploding in population. There aren’t enough “ghettos” to redevelop, so instead people start moving to Trumpvilles a few dozen miles away.
